text:
Predicates:
Rabbit(x) ::: x is a rabbit.
Turtle(x) ::: x is a turtle.
Squirrel(x) ::: x is a squirrel.
SpottedNearCampus(x) ::: x can be spotted near the campus.
Cute(x) ::: x is cute.
Skittish(x) ::: x is skittish.
Calm(x) ::: x is calm.
Rockie ::: Rockie.

Premises:
∀x ((Rabbit(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) → Cute(x)) ::: All rabbits that can be spotted near the campus are cute.
∃x (Turtle(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) ::: Some turtles can be spotted near the campus.
∀x (SpottedNearCampus(x) → (Rabbit(x) ∨ Squirrel(x))) ::: The only animals that can be spotted near the campus are rabbits and squirrels.
∀x (Skittish(x) → ¬Calm(x)) ::: If something is skittish, then it is not calm.
∀x ((Squirrel(x) ∧ SpottedNearCampus(x)) → Skittish(x)) ::: All the squirrels that can be spotted near the campus are skittish.
SpottedNearCampus(Rockie) ∧ Calm(Rockie) ::: Rockie can be spotted near the campus, and it is calm.

Conclusion:
¬(Turtle(Rockie) ∧ Squirrel(Rockie)) → (Cute(Rockie) ∨ Skittish(Rockie)) ::: If Rockie is not both a turtle and a squirrel, then Rockie is either cute or skittish.
